title: Energy, Damping and Resonance
welcome_lead: Trade kinetic for potential energy in an oscillator, then watch damping eat the amplitude.
meta_desc: A-Level Further Mechanics adventure on energy in SHM, damping and resonance.
final_note: Drive a lightly damped system at its natural frequency and you'll get resonance.

walkthroughs.body_html: At equilibrium: all KE. At amplitude: all PE. Total energy E = ½ k A² stays constant in an ideal oscillator. KE + PE = constant.
Light damping: amplitude decays exponentially. Heavy damping: very slow return to equilibrium, no oscillation. Critical damping: fastest return without overshoot.
When driving frequency equals natural frequency, amplitude grows large. Less damping = sharper, taller resonance peak. Examples: tuning forks, bridges, AC circuits.
